title: Solid-state electronics resources and shop checklist
summary: A manufacturer-led reference shelf, datasheet reading sequence and final worksheet for taking the course into careful component review.

blocks.title: Use the course as a map, then read the selected part
blocks.body: Application notes explain families and methods. Only the exact device datasheet, errata and manufacturer updates define the selected part. Record document revisions and test conditions with every design decision.

blocks.heading: 1. A repeatable datasheet reading sequence
items: Confirm the exact orderable part, package, marking and datasheet revision.
Read the recommended operating context and feature summary without treating marketing bullets as limits.
Mark absolute maximum ratings as boundaries. Then find the separate electrical-characteristic rows that guarantee performance.
Carry every rating’s test conditions, temperature and pulse duration into your notes.
Read graphs as typical guidance unless the document explicitly guarantees them.
Check package drawing, pinout, thermal information, safe operating area and application notes.
Write what remains unverified and define the measurement that will close it.

blocks.heading: 2. Know what each source can support

columns.name: Exact manufacturer datasheet
columns.detail: Ratings, guaranteed electrical characteristics, package and ordering identity for one device. Check revision and conditions.

columns.name: Manufacturer application note
columns.detail: Models, selection methods and example circuits. Useful context, but examples do not override the chosen device datasheet.

columns.name: Distributor page
columns.detail: Helpful for availability and document discovery. Confirm technical facts against the manufacturer source.

columns.name: Forum, video or blog
columns.detail: Can expose useful questions and failure modes. Treat claims as leads until primary evidence or controlled measurement supports them.

items.label: Define the function
items.detail: State what the device controls and why this topology fits.

items.label: List normal stresses
items.detail: Voltage, current, frequency, temperature, duty cycle and timing.

items.label: List abnormal stresses
items.detail: Startup, shutdown, open load, short, surge, reversed polarity and loss of control.

items.label: Verify the driver
items.detail: Reference, amplitude, source and sink current, timing, default state and isolation.

items.label: Verify protection
items.detail: Clamp path, fuse or current limit, transient margin and energy rating.

items.label: Verify thermal path
items.detail: Loss assumptions, package, board or sink, interface, ambient and junction estimate.

items.label: Plan evidence
items.detail: Waveforms, temperatures, timing, load cases and review authority needed before release.

blocks.title: A worksheet is not approval
blocks.body: Completing these prompts does not certify a circuit, machine modification or safety function. Competent review, applicable standards and controlled verification remain necessary.

blocks.heading: Course source: semiconductor, diode and BJT basics
blocks.source: Toshiba — Basic Knowledge of Discrete Semiconductor Devices
blocks.caption: Chapters I–III provide the manufacturer tutorials used for carrier, junction, diode and transistor foundations. Accessed 2026-09-21.

blocks.heading: Course source: rectifier fundamentals
blocks.caption: Background on forward and reverse behavior, recovery and loss. Accessed 2026-09-21.

blocks.heading: Course source: gate-drive fundamentals
blocks.source: Texas Instruments — SLUA618A, Fundamentals of MOSFET and IGBT Gate Driver Circuits
blocks.caption: Detailed MOSFET switching intervals, gate charge and driver relationships. Accessed 2026-09-21.

blocks.heading: Course source: power MOSFET selection
blocks.source: Texas Instruments — Avoid Common Mistakes When Selecting and Designing With Power MOSFETs
blocks.caption: Practical warnings about specifications, gate drive, thermal design and safe operating area. Accessed 2026-09-21.

blocks.heading: Course source: inductive discharge
blocks.source: Texas Instruments — SNVAA45, inductive discharge application brief
blocks.caption: Background on coil energy, freewheel and clamp tradeoffs. Accessed 2026-09-21.

blocks.heading: Finish with an evidence-backed handoff
blocks.body: Name the part, conditions, remaining uncertainty, review boundary and next controlled test. If another person cannot reconstruct why a rating applies, the handoff is not finished.
